theory: Literature acquisition turns versioned external paper bytes into immutable, locally checkable records. Search results are leads, admitted metadata and source archives are evidence, and citations retain the identity of what was read. Shared throttling describes the external service caller rather than one project.
instead_of: A search-and-download convenience layer misses immutable version identity, read-time digest verification, whole-archive admission, and the distinction between a search lead and admitted source.

absorption.rationale: Versions, transport replacements, and machine-wide budgets fit; non-arXiv papers lack first-class identity because PaperRecord and library paths require ArxivId.

world_mapping.rationale: Versioned identifiers, record bytes, response identity, manifests, and citation provenance model distinguishable evidence. The cache is machine-local while bibliography identity travels.

abstraction.rationale: Metadata values, transport, immutable library, and archive admission have separate owners. Injected transport/clock/sleep expose temporal acquisition rules without real network calls.

justification.rationale: Code explains why throttling belongs above project roots and provenance belongs inside digested content. Tests refuse hostile archives whole and prevent serving modified admitted bytes.

honest_limits.rationale: Search results are not admitted records, unversioned records cannot be held, and HTTP deadline code states best-effort socket narrowing and possible overshoot.

rehearsals.requirement: Fetch a later version without changing an old citation's bytes.
rehearsals.why: Versioned ArxivId and immutable storage naturally distinguish both records.

rehearsals.requirement: Apply one request clock to several project caches.
rehearsals.why: PaperLibrary accepts a separate throttle directory; the client receives interval and clock explicitly.

rehearsals.requirement: Admit and cite a DOI-only journal paper with no arXiv identity.
rehearsals.why: DOI is metadata beside required arxiv_id; identifier reparses that field as ArxivId, requiring a provider-neutral identity across record/storage APIs.
